% note: Every comparison is exploratory, unadjusted and outside the Holm family: no verdict is printed. The status column repeats each block's stamped label.
% note: The own-$k$ votes use each Haiku setting's own cost-matched $k$ against Opus-medium and against Sonnet-medium; where a $k$ is capped, the Raw $k$ column gives the cost-matched $k$ before the cap. Capped, all against Opus-medium: Haiku-low on 6\ensuremath{\times}1, held at the cap on $k$ of 40 (raw $k$ 46); Haiku, thinking off on 1\ensuremath{\times}6 and 6\ensuremath{\times}1, held at the cap on $k$ of 40 (raw $k$ 45 and 50); Haiku-max on 1\ensuremath{\times}6 and 6\ensuremath{\times}1, held at its 3 samples drawn (raw $k$ 9 and 11). Against Sonnet-medium no $k$ is capped. The spend share of a vote is its spend over the comparator's (the file's ``spend ratio''), a point with no interval.
% note: Spend shares print at three decimals; 0.9998 (Haiku-low vote against Opus-medium at 1\ensuremath{\times}6) keeps a fourth decimal, because at three it would print as 1.000 and read as equal to the comparator's spend.
% note: The pieces counterparts repeat Test~3's and Test~5's comparisons at 6\ensuremath{\times}1. Test~4's comparison was not computed at 6\ensuremath{\times}1 in the main run, because step voting did not run on pieces there. Step voting on pieces against one Opus-medium answer (the pieces counterpart of Test~4; unadjusted, exploratory, outside the pre-registered family) ran later, in the top-up run, and is reported in ⟦TAB-14⟧.
% note: Neither pieces counterpart is shown no worse (Holm-adjusted): both are outside the Holm family. The file's own ``declared'' field on the counterpart of Test~5 means its $p$ fell below the one-sided level for that comparison alone, not under Holm, and is not shown.
% note: Format compliance is the share of each side's samples in the required answer format; for a vote, that of the setting's samples the vote is drawn from.
% note: Effort pairs are low effort minus medium effort at one sample; the cost difference is the stamped difference of the two mean list costs of one sample (in US dollars; for Opus, its one answer).
% note: Where both settings of an effort pair are at the ceiling, the bootstrap interval of $d$ collapses to one point (marked collapsed). The difference itself has no exact interval in free analysis 4, which gives each setting's exact 95\% interval instead (Clopper--Pearson over puzzles), printed in that setting's accuracy cell as post hoc\ensuremath{^{\dagger}} (exact): a presentation only, not a test.
% note: Opus-low against Sonnet-medium at 1\ensuremath{\times}6 is Test~5's comparison. Its confirmatory $d$ and interval are in ⟦TAB-02⟧; the Opus-against-Sonnet block's separate exploratory interval for the same pair is not printed, and that row keeps the block's accuracies and cost ratios only. At 6\ensuremath{\times}1 the same pair is the pieces counterpart of Test~5: its $d$ and interval are printed once, in that row, and the Opus-against-Sonnet row keeps its accuracies and cost ratios only.
% note: Dashes mark cells that do not apply (a spend share and a raw $k$ belong to the votes, a cost ratio to the Opus-against-Sonnet rows), cells the files do not stamp (the $k$ of the Opus-against-Sonnet rows and of the pieces counterpart of Test~5, and the cost difference in dollars of the Opus-against-Sonnet rows) and the $d$ cells of the two Opus-against-Sonnet rows whose comparison is printed elsewhere. The cost columns are in a part of their own that prints only the rows with a cost figure, so the dashes of the other rows are not printed there; the accuracy columns are in two parts, one for the own-$k$ votes and one for the other rows.
% note: Sonnet-medium ran at medium effort, one level below Sonnet's default, in every row where it appears.
